prompt_text:
Task: Static Image and Visual Understanding

Write code that detects text appearing inside an image using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Azure AI Vision:
  Service: Azure AI Vision
  SDK: azure-ai-vision-imageanalysis / REST
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: analyze
  Setup hints: AZURE_VISION_ENDPOINT, AZURE_VISION_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/computer-vision/overview-image-analysis

Option 2 — Clarifai:
  Service: Clarifai Image Recognition
  SDK: clarifai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: predict
  Setup hints: CLARIFAI_PAT
  Official docs: https://docs.clarifai.com/api-guide/predict/images

Option 3 — Google Cloud Vision:
  Service: Cloud Vision
  SDK: google-cloud-vision
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: label_detection, text_detection
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/vision/docs

Option 4 — Amazon Rekognition:
  Service: Amazon Rekognition
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: detect_labels, detect_text
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/what-is.html

Option 5 — Qwen-VL / Alibaba visual understanding:
  Service: DashScope multimodal vision
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: MultiModalConversation.call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-vl-api

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
from google.cloud import vision
import io

def detect_text_in_image(image_bytes: bytes) -> list[str]:
    """
    Detects text in an image using Google Cloud Vision API.

    Args:
        image_bytes: The image content as bytes.

    Returns:
        A list of strings, where each string is a block of detected text.
    """
    <GAP>
    client = vision.ImageAnnotatorClient()

    image = vision.Image(content=image_bytes)

    response = client.text_detection(image=image)
    texts = response.text_annotations

    detected_strings = []
    # The first text annotation is the overall detected text, subsequent ones are individual words/lines.
    # We'll return the description from all annotations except the first (which is often the entire text).
    # If there's at least one annotation (the full text), we'll add it.
    if texts:
        # The full text is usually in the first annotation's description
        # Let's return the full text and then individual lines/words for more granular results if needed.
        # For this task, returning all detected text blocks is appropriate.
        for text in texts:
            detected_strings.append(text.description)
    
    # Often, the very first annotation contains the entire detected text.
    # If we want to return just individual blocks/words, we might skip texts[0]
    # For now, let's return all unique descriptions found.
    # To avoid duplicates if the first entry is just a concatenation of others,
    # let's collect unique descriptions after the first one which is usually the 'full text'.
    
    unique_descriptions = []
    if texts:
        # Add the full text if it exists
        unique_descriptions.append(texts[0].description)
        # Add descriptions of other text annotations (individual words/lines), ensuring uniqueness
        for i in range(1, len(texts)):
            if texts[i].description not in unique_descriptions:
                unique_descriptions.append(texts[i].description)

    # Handle potential errors from the API call
    if response.error.message:
        raise Exception(
            f"{response.error.message}\nFor more info on error messages, check: "
            f"https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors"
        )

    return unique_descriptions
